title: Model-Visible Representation Taxonomy for Generative Biological Foundation Model Routes
classification_unit: One grounded input route: the path from a biological or textual source object through transformations to the model-visible form consumed by a generative multimodal biological foundation model.
organizing_principle: The primary hierarchy groups routes by the model-visible representation mechanism. Biological modality, lifecycle phase, fusion topology, text role, and route status are treated as orthogonal dimensions rather than top-level categories.

families.name: Direct Text Tokens
families.definition: Routes whose visible carrier is ordinary language text or prompt scaffolding, with no domain-specific biological serialization or learned biological embedding inserted before the model sees it.
families.structural_criterion: The model consumes standard prompt text, question text, instruction text, or retrieval-style task text as text tokens.

leaves.name: Plain Language Prompts
leaves.definition: Natural-language prompts or questions that are not first converted into a biological serialization, embedding prefix, image, or discrete biological token stream.
include_when: the source object is already presented as ordinary prose or question text
the route is a direct prompt without biological serialization
exclude_when: the biological source is first serialized into gene lists, cell sentences, or structured omics templates
the visible form is a learned embedding prefix or an image token stream

leaves.name: Instruction Or Question Scaffolds
leaves.definition: Prompt text whose decisive structure is an explicit instruction, question, conversation turn, or benchmark-style scaffold around the biological task.
include_when: the route is framed as instruction tuning, question answering, or conversational prompting
the model-visible form is standard language text with task scaffolding
exclude_when: the visible carrier is a biological serialization such as a cell sentence or gene list
the prompt is replaced by a learned prefix or image representation

leaves.name: Retrieval Or Tool Style Prompts
leaves.definition: Prompt text whose function is retrieval, ranking, task-definition injection, or other tool-like natural-language control rather than direct biological serialization.
include_when: the prompt specifies a retrieval or ranking task over entities
the route uses task-definition text as the visible carrier
exclude_when: the route is primarily a biological serialization such as a gene list or cell sentence
the route is a learned embedding or rasterized image

families.name: Serialized Biological Text
families.definition: Routes where biological objects are rendered into text strings that preserve domain structure, such as cell sentences, gene lists, ranked profiles, metadata templates, or labeled sequence templates.
families.structural_criterion: The model-visible form is a text serialization of biological content rather than raw prose prompt text.

leaves.name: Cell Or Gene Sentence Serializations
leaves.definition: Cell-level or neighborhood-level biological content serialized as sentences or sentence-like token sequences.
include_when: source objects are converted into cell sentences, spatial sentences, or gene-centered sentence forms
the route preserves biological ordering or neighborhood context in textual form
exclude_when: the route remains plain prompt text without biological serialization
the visible carrier is an embedding prefix or image raster

leaves.name: Structured Metadata And Placeholder Prompts
leaves.definition: Biological metadata rendered into structured text fields, placeholder-bearing prompts, or template-like task frames that expose explicit field structure.
include_when: the route uses metadata fields, placeholders, or structured task blocks
the biological content is explicitly formatted into a prompt template
exclude_when: the route is only ordinary prose prompt text
the route is a learned embedding or a discrete latent token stream

leaves.name: Ranked Or Quantitative Profile Serializations
leaves.definition: Textual routes whose visible form is a ranked, ordered, or otherwise quantitative biological profile rendered as text.
include_when: the route is expressed as ranked gene lists, ordered expression hierarchies, or text-based quantitative profile prompts
the textual form is directly tied to expression or perturbation ordering
exclude_when: the route is an embedding prefix or image patch representation
the route is a generic prose prompt with no biological serialization

leaves.name: Identifier Labeled Sequence Templates
leaves.definition: Sequence generation routes where the visible input is a template combining an identifier or class label with a sequence placeholder.
include_when: the route uses explicit templates such as species, tRNA, rRNA, or histone labels plus a sequence placeholder
the biological object is represented textually before generation
exclude_when: the route is a latent embedding prefix or a raw image input
the route is only a plain prompt without a biological template

families.name: Learned Continuous Prefixes
families.definition: Routes where the source object is encoded by a learned model and injected as continuous vectors, prefixes, query tokens, or soft prompts in the language-model context.
families.structural_criterion: The visible form is a projected embedding, query token block, soft prefix, or other continuous vector representation.

leaves.name: Transcriptome Or Cell Embeddings
leaves.definition: Continuous vectors derived from transcriptomes, cells, or omics profiles and inserted into the language model context.
include_when: the source is transcriptomic or cell-level biological content projected into embedding space
the route uses query tokens, virtual tokens, or adapter-fed embeddings for omics content
exclude_when: the visible form is a plain text cell sentence or gene list
the route is a rasterized image or a discrete token stream

leaves.name: Sequence Or Molecule Embeddings
leaves.definition: Continuous vectors derived from protein, DNA, RNA, peptide, small-molecule, or other molecular sequence content and injected into the language model context.
include_when: the route passes through a modality-specific encoder and then into a unified prompt or prefix
the visible form is a projected sequence or molecular embedding
exclude_when: the route remains a plain text sequence template
the route is only a discrete tokenized corpus

leaves.name: Image Embeddings Or Virtual Tokens
leaves.definition: Continuous visual embeddings or virtual tokens projected from histology, microscopy, or other image inputs into the language model context.
include_when: the source is an image or image patch encoder feeding virtual tokens or projected features
the model-visible form is a fixed number of virtual tokens or conditioning features
exclude_when: the route is a raw image fed directly into a vision stack without projection into language context
the route is a non-visual text or discrete token input

families.name: Visual Raster Tokens
families.definition: Routes where the model-visible form is a raster image, image patch, slide tile, or other visual tensor rather than a text or embedding prefix.
families.structural_criterion: The visible carrier is a rasterized image or image-patch input consumed by a vision encoder or visual branch.

leaves.name: Histology Or Microscopy Rasters
leaves.definition: Raw microscopy, histology, or pathology image patches processed as visual tensors.
include_when: the input is an H&E, DAPI, or other microscopy image patch
the route uses raw visual evidence rather than a projected embedding prefix
exclude_when: the image is first converted into a virtual-token prefix
the route is a text-only or discrete-token input

families.name: Discrete Symbolic Tokens
families.definition: Routes where biological content is first converted into discrete token sequences, tokenized corpora, or learned symbolic atoms before the model consumes it.
families.structural_criterion: The visible form is a tokenized biological corpus or an atomized biological vocabulary rather than a continuous embedding or raster image.

leaves.name: Tokenized Cell Sentence Sequences
leaves.definition: Cell-level or spatial sentence content converted into discrete token sequences.
include_when: the visible form is a tokenized cell sentence, spatial sentence, or multi-cell sentence
the route serializes biological context into discrete sentence tokens
exclude_when: the route is a plain prompt without biological sentence content
the route is a learned continuous prefix or a raw image

leaves.name: Tokenized Sequence Corpora
leaves.definition: General biological sequence corpora converted into discrete BPE, tokenizer, or chunked token streams.
include_when: the source is DNA, RNA, protein, or related sequence text tokenized into discrete chunks
the route uses an extended tokenizer or chunked sequence corpus
exclude_when: the sequence is only represented as a continuous embedding
the route is an image or plain language prompt

leaves.name: Atomic Gene Symbol Tokens
leaves.definition: Routes where gene symbols or similar canonical biological tokens are treated as atomic vocabulary items rather than subword fragments.
include_when: the tokenizer vocabulary is explicitly augmented with biological symbols
gene names are treated as atomic tokens during instruction tuning
exclude_when: the route uses generic prompt text without vocabulary augmentation
the route is a continuous embedding prefix or a discrete sequence corpus

families.name: Graph Or Relation Conditioning
families.definition: Routes where the source is a pathway, interaction network, or other relation structure that is exposed as graph reasoning text or as graph-derived context rather than as a flat prompt alone.
families.structural_criterion: The visible mechanism is graph reasoning context, relation metadata, or graph-shaped task definition.

leaves.name: Graph Reasoning Text Prompts
leaves.definition: Natural-language prompts that encode graph reasoning tasks such as reachability, shortest paths, pathway completion, or interaction reasoning.
include_when: the task asks for graph or pathway reasoning in text form
the visible carrier is a graph-derived question, instruction, or prompt block
exclude_when: the route only uses generic prose prompt text with no graph content
the route is a graph embedding or a continuous prefix

leaves.name: Graph Derived Context Tokens
leaves.definition: Routes where graph or relation structure is compressed into a context token stream or graph-derived representation for model use.
include_when: the graph is converted into a tokenized relation context or graph-derived model input
the source is pathway, PPI, or interaction structure that becomes model-visible context
exclude_when: the route remains ordinary non-graph text
the route is a raster image or a generic continuous embedding unrelated to relation structure

families.name: State Or Noise Conditioning
families.definition: Routes where the model-visible form is a perturbed state, noise state, masked context, or counterfactual delta representation rather than an ordinary semantic prompt.
families.structural_criterion: The visible carrier is a diffusion state, masked context, or counterfactual state variable.

leaves.name: Diffusion Or Noise States
leaves.definition: Routes that expose noisy latents, forward or reverse diffusion states, or other stochastic generative states to the model.
include_when: the route uses noisy coordinates, diffusion time steps, or a forward or reverse generative state
the visible carrier is a latent state rather than semantic text
exclude_when: the route is a plain text prompt or a biological serialization
the route is a static image or discrete token corpus

leaves.name: Masked Or Delta Contexts
leaves.definition: Routes that expose masked, partially removed, or counterfactual perturbation contexts as the model-visible representation.
include_when: the route randomly masks prompt identifiers or otherwise hides part of the conditioning context
the route uses delta-style or counterfactual perturbation representations as visible input
exclude_when: the route is ordinary prompt text without masking or perturbation state
the route is a diffusion latent or a static biological serialization

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Biological Modality
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The underlying source domain, independent of how it is represented to the model.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Lifecycle Phase
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: Where in the model lifecycle the route occurs.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Text Role
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The role played by text in the route, independent of the representation mechanism.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Fusion Topology
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: How the route is inserted into or combined with the generative model.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Route Status
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: Whether the route is an actual input, a training-only target, a generated output, or a non-primary comparison route.

category_errors_prevented: Treating a paper or benchmark as one category instead of classifying each route separately.
Collapsing actual inputs, training-only targets, generated outputs, baselines, and ablations into the same bucket.
Using hybrid as a catch-all instead of the visible representation mechanism.
Classifying by biology alone rather than by the model-visible form.
Merging plain prompt text with serialized biological text or with learned continuous prefixes.
Confusing postprocessing outputs with input routes.
Letting ungrounded or unclear states create taxonomy categories.
Mixing lifecycle phase with representation mechanism.
unresolved_questions: Whether delta-style perturbation routes should remain a separate leaf from ranked profile serializations in the final corpus coding pass.
Whether graph-derived textual prompts should stay separate from other structured metadata prompts once the inventory is expanded beyond this excerpt.
Whether token-augmented biological vocabularies should remain a discrete-token leaf or be folded into a broader serialized-text leaf in later annotation sweeps.
